system.summary: Graphic substitution alphabet with homophones, signs for doubled letters (tt, ss, ff, ll) and name signs. The queen's two letters use few homophones (a, o, u, n) and two name signs (King of Hungary, Venetians); the king's letter uses the same values with more signs for e (three), i, u/v, g and s, and name signs for King Ferdinand, the Duke of Ferrara and the Emperor.
system.notes: The 1482 alphabet looks different from those of the 1486 letters (RESULT.md); R1142 (March 1486) says it uses the old cipher and encloses a new one. Split 14 Oct 2026: R1142 is beatrice1486, R1143 beatrice1486b, R1154 (not a cipher) beatrice1505. Key rebuilt 14 Nov 2026 from the Vestigia cipher/clear pairs (vestigia/README.md). The king's letter R1156 (former target matthias1482) folded in on 14 Nov 2026 after 9 = d and 2 = g were confirmed on its image (NOTES, 'Fold of matthias1482'). distinct_symbols counts the queen's letters only.

prior_solution.where: Nagy-Nyáry, Magyar Diplomácziai Emlékek III (1877), nos. 10 and 12, with the cipher passages set in italics; for R1156 the same volume (no. 11 by Vestigia's record) and Fraknói, Mátyás király levelei II (1895) no. 131. Period clear copies of all three letters on Vestigia (1958, 1961, 2627).

conditions.human_role: Supplied target catalogue entry and pointed out available DECODE cookie. For R1156 (project-level): obtained a DECODE login and passed its session token to the model.
tools: Python alignment and Levenshtein scoring (vestigia/train_key.py, measure.py)

solution.what: R1156 (then the target matthias1482): DECODE record R1156 and its two images fetched with a login.
R1156 (then the target matthias1482): Found the letter printed in full in MDE III (1877) no. 14 and Fraknoi II (1895) no. 131, from the Modena original.
R1156 (then the target matthias1482): Working key rebuilt from the cipher runs aligned with the printed text, each value checked on at least two words; three name signs identified.

R1156 (then the target matthias1482): Every run read from the glyphs; four corrections to the print (valent, gentibus, the closing 'Speramus cito nos res nostras ita disposituros...', and the 'contemporary regest' shown to be the letter's own half-ciphered last sentence).
R1156 (then the target matthias1482): 'illic faciet [q-sign] venient' against printed 'convenire', and two signs after 'regina' on line 3, left unresolved.
Extracted five exact dates, recipients and shelfmarks from cached DECODE metadata; web reader could not open live DECODE page.
Used existing user-authorized DECODE cookie to acquire all 18 images. R1143 has repeated photographs with decipherment slips moved.
Located MDE III nos. 10 and 12 for both 1482 letters, III no. 75 for May 1486, IV supplement no. 45 for March cipher and III no. 54 for its closing.

Matched dates, clear wording, cipher boundaries and R1143 manuscript slips to older readings. Rendered print confirms italics and March Virtus/Fortis/M. markers. No exhaustive key verification claimed.
Visual inspection of MDE III p. 17 corrects OCR holla to printed balla. Preserve machine extracts as uncorrected evidence.

Entry split under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): the 1482 letters R1140 and R1141 keep this entry; R1142 and R1143 (1486, alphabets that look different, and R1142 announces a new cipher) and the plain letter R1154 have their own entries.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): the OCR extracts of the 1877 printed decipherments (MDE III nos. 10, 12) as decryptions; no glyph transcription of either cipher exists (project work).

R1156 (then the target matthias1482): Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): the letter with its cipher runs as read from the glyphs (NOTES.md, copied to texts/R1156_decryption.md), Fraknói's 1895 printed text extracted from fraknoi_v2.txt (texts/R1156_fraknoi1895.txt), and the rebuilt key copied from NOTES.md (texts/key.md); the glyph sequence itself was never written out, so there is no transcription (project work)

Vestigia's period clear copies (1958, 1961) paired with the cipher originals (1957, 1960). Key K_V rebuilt from R1140 only, frozen by SHA-256 after a pre-registration, measured once on the whole of R1141 (648 signs, blind transcription): characters 0.900, precision 0.867, words 0.644, against best 0.290 of 200 keys shuffled within value classes; threshold 0.85 and +0.30 passed. Restores a cipher run of R1141 left out of the 1877 print ('Venetiani da sua offesa'). Same alphabet as matthias1482 (17 shared values, 2 contradictions).

Integration check of PR #620. measure.py re-run with the relabel argument: 0.900 / 0.867 / 0.644, controls best 0.290 (0.891 without the relabelling); hashes of PREREG.md and K_V.json match; own scorer 0.901 against at most 0.346. train_key.py is seeded with 9 = d and 2 = g; re-run without them: 2 = g 10/10, 9 = d 29/33. matthias1482's values on R1141: 9 = e with 2 = d 0.833, with 2 = i 0.843. Vestigia images opened: 62 signs of R1141 agree with the transcription; the margin of the clear copy 1961 has the restored run. Key partial (three shapes without a value, 8 signs, and one unread sign). Order of events by the contributor's record. Guerra 2010 (listed by Vestigia) not opened.

R1156 (then the target matthias1482): Comparison with the key rebuilt for beatrice1482 (PR #620, Brice Dudout): sixteen letter values and the sign for the King of Hungary agree (seventeen values), three differ (d: 2 here, 9 there; g: hooked L here, 2 there; e: 5, 4, 9, ς here, one 5-like sign there). On R1141, held out, 9 = d and 2 = g give 0.900 against 0.833-0.843 for this key's values. Not settled for R1156: no sign-level transcription in this folder, images behind the DECODE login. Key left unchanged; open point in NOTES. Same key as beatrice1482 by the evidence; not folded (owner's decision).

R1156: Vestigia searched for the king's letter. Found with open images, no login: document 2626 (cipher original, DF 295613) and 2627 (a clear copy of the time, DF 295614), not known to the project before.

R1156: the cipher runs of Vestigia 2626 transcribed sign by sign with the clear copy beside it (not blind): 69 runs, 409 signs, 12 of them name signs (matthias1482/vestigia/R1156_V2626_transcription.txt).

Same-key question decided on R1156 itself. d is a 9-form in 8 of 8 places (the head unclear in two); g is the figure 2 in Mager and quingentos (an L-form in four other places); the Venetians' and the king's signs are those of the queen's letters. K_V as it stands recovers 283 of 399 letters of the clear copy (0.709), with the signs only this letter has 389 of 399 (0.975); the earlier key's 9 = e and 2 = d give 379 (0.950), losing all ten deciding places. Not a held-out test, no controls. Verdict: one key; the king's letter uses more homophones. The earlier key of R1156 corrected on d, g, e, i and the Venetians' sign.

R1156 re-read against the period clear copy (Vestigia 2627): electos added after quingentos; 'significet Regi Hungarie et illic faciet quod venient' settled; more runs marked as cipher; the copy reads sentibus where the sense wants gentibus; valent, the Speramus sentence and the closing sentence were already in the copy of the time. Two signs after regina still unread.

matthias1482 folded into this entry under the one-key rule (owner's decision, conditional on the same key): folder moved to matthias1482/ with its notes and profile kept beside it; the page docs/matthias1482.html replaced by a moved-page notice.

outcome.method_basis: All three letters were already deciphered in print: Magyar Diplomácziai Emlékek III (1877), nos. 10 and 12 for the queen's letters, the same volume and Fraknói 1895 no. 131 for the king's. The prints were matched to the images; the king's letter was also re-read from its signs.
outcome.notes: Matthias's offer of Swiss and cavalry against Venice for money paid at Milan, and his own letter to Ercole on the 500 horse he cannot get through. Split on 14 Oct 2026 from the five-record group. 14 Nov 2026: key rebuilt and validated on a held-out letter; one cipher run of R1141 missing from the 1877 print restored; the king's letter R1156 (former target matthias1482) folded in after its d and g were checked on Vestigia's image.

texts.label: Pozsony, 31 May 1482
texts.summary: Beatrice of Aragon writes to her sister Eleonora, Duchess of Ferrara, during the War of Ferrara: for 100,000 ducats sent to Milan, King Matthias would raise 16,000 men (10,000 Swiss and 6,000 cavalry) in the Brescia and Verona districts against Venice, but will not declare himself openly before his relations with the league are settled. Decryption: uncorrected OCR of the printed decipherment in Magyar Diplomácziai Emlékek III (1877) no. 10.

texts.label: Pozsony, 8 June 1482
texts.summary: Beatrice reports Matthias's displeasure at the league's unwillingness to spend, repeats the Swiss and cavalry offer, asks for money to be sent to Milan and calls for action rather than negotiations that keep 'returning to the beginning' like a ball game. Decryption: uncorrected OCR of MDE III (1877) no. 12.

reading_review.note: The corrected sentence read against the margin of the period clear copy (Vestigia 1961, image opened): 'et tale che non solamente havia tolto Venetiani da sua offesa ma li haria ridocti a carastia de defenderse'. The rest of the reading is the 1877 print as before; not re-read in full against the copy. The contributor's own review (same date) reported the same correction.

texts.label: Matthias to Ercole I d'Este, Pozsony, 1 June 1482
texts.summary: King Matthias Corvinus to Duke Ercole I of Ferrara, his brother-in-law, in the first weeks of the War of Ferrara: he and Queen Beatrix had resolved to send 500 picked horse, among them 100 hussars, but found no safe road; his captain Balázs Magyar goes to Croatia towards the Venetian border to gather troops. Printed by Fraknói (1895, no. 131); re-read from the signs and against the clear copy of the time.

parts.label: The text of the three letters
parts.basis: Printed decipherments in MDE III (1877) and Fraknói 1895 no. 131; one run of R1141 missing from the print restored from the period clear copy (Vestigia 1961); R1156 re-read from its signs and against its period clear copy (Vestigia 2627).

parts.label: The 1482 key
parts.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
parts.basis: Brice Dudout (PR #620): rebuilt from R1140 aligned on its period clear copy and the print, measured on R1141 held out (0.900 against 0.290 for shuffled keys; order of events by the contributor's record); three shapes without a value. Its values 9 = d and 2 = g confirmed on R1156 (14 Nov 2026), whose further signs were added from that letter and its clear copy.
